messages:
Omar R: @eng-security quick FYI: during an access audit we discovered an archived backup (internal repo backup) that contains a user's private SSH keys. The backup was accessible to a small set of contractors. No evidence of exfiltration yet, but those keys had user access to the bastion and some deploy hosts. Immediate rotation required.

Omar R: TL;DR: rotate user keys, rotate any deploy keys that accepted the user key, remove the compromised pubkey from authorized_keys on affected hosts, enable short-lived SSH certs for contractors. Confirm in-thread when done.

security-oncall: Automated scan flagged 3 private keys in archive `repo-backups/2025-11-02.tar.gz`. We created ticket SEC-7345 and temporarily disabled contractor accounts that had access. Full owner list sent via DM.

Priya S: Which hosts are affected? Do we need a bastion maintenance window?

Omar R: Affected: bastion-nyc-1, deploy-02, and analytics-worker-7. We recommend a rolling quick maintenance to remove keys and restart sshd where needed. Not customer impacting but plan for ~10m per host.

eng-sre: Quick commands to remediate:

```
# remove pubkey from authorized_keys
ssh ops@bastion-nyc-1 'grep -v "ssh-rsa AAAA...oldkey" ~/.ssh/authorized_keys > /tmp/ak && mv /tmp/ak ~/.ssh/authorized_keys && chown ops:ops ~/.ssh/authorized_keys'
# restart sshd if you changed host config
sudo systemctl restart sshd || sudo service ssh restart
# verify last logins
sudo last -n 50 | head -n 20
```

eng-sre: Also run `ssh-cert-check --host bastion-nyc-1 --list` to see certificate-based logins and revoke certs issued to compromised identity.

infra-bot: Created infra ticket INFRA-4881 to run an automated grep across host authorized_keys and report matches. Link: https://redwood.internal/t/INFRA-4881

security-oncall: Checklist: 1) rotate the compromised user's SSH keys and revoke old keys 2) remove any matching pubkeys from authorized_keys on affected hosts 3) rotate any deploy keys or CI secrets that accepted the user key 4) disable contractor accounts until certs/keys are rotated 5) enable short-lived SSH certs via our SSH CA for contractors and external contributors 6) attach evidence (screenshots or command output) to SEC-7345.

ops-lead: We'll coordinate rolling restarts. Ops will take bastion-nyc-1 first at 23:30 UTC, then deploy-02, then analytics-worker-7. Expect ~30m total.

Priya S: Rotated user keys for the impacted account and updated Vault entry at secret/ssh/users/omar-legacy. Removed the pubkey from bastion-nyc-1 and restarted sshd. Test logins ok.

Omar R: Thanks Priya. Please paste output of `ssh-keygen -lf` for the new key or a Vault read screenshot so we can mark SEC-7345 resolved for that user.

eng-sre: Ran automated scan across fleet; found two additional hosts with the pubkey. We removed them and restarted sshd. Report attached to INFRA-4881.

security-oncall: If teams still using long-lived user keys for automation, migrate to signed certs and short-lived tokens. We'll publish a policy update next week requiring certs for non-org-owned machines.

Priya S: Confirmed all affected hosts remediated and contractor accounts disabled. Evidence uploaded to SEC-7345.

Omar R: Closing the loop 1: no signs of active misuse, rotations complete, infra scan clear. We'll follow up with a short postmortem and policy change requiring SSH CA for contractor access by Q3. Thanks all.
